newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise, confound market players.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise, confound market players.

text.p: Argentine bonds were higher late Friday, confounding market players who were struggling to explain the rise in the face of sharp losses in U.S. bonds.
"This is completely contrary to what I expected," said one analyst at a foreign bank.
U.S. Treasuries plummetted after the release of a strong December jobs report. The U.S. 30-year bond yield was last 10 basis points higher at 6.85 percent.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 1/2 to 87-3/8, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.35 to 124.20.
Even Argentina's fixed-rate Par bond due 2023, usually the most sensitive to U.S. long bond declines, recovered nearly all its early losses to finish a mere 1/8 lower at 62-1/4.
"I can't find a logical reason for it," said another analyst.
One explanation, suggested the first analyst, was that "investors have been pleased by the government's policy of covering the year's debt as quickly as possible."

The government will already have placed $5.0 billion of its $8.5 billion planned foreign issues for 1997 by the end of March when it issues $3.0 billion worth of global bonds announced earlier this week.

Another explanation, suggested the second analyst, is that the market is correcting in the anticipation of the pricing of the $2.0 billion five- and 20-year bonds in the second half of January. The five-year issue is seen priced at 300 basis points over Treasuries while the 20-year bond is seen at less than 450 basis points over, said the analyst.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 5.65 percent from 5.48 percent.
